title: inference-positioning-playbook-v1
body:
Purpose
A compact, battle-tested narrative we can hand to SDRs, product-marketing, and solutions engineers. Focus: explain why engineering-first customers choose Redwood for production LLM inference (not research/model training). This is a working playbook — surface feedback, iterate.

Core thesis (one line)
Serving is the new moat: teams win by making inference predictable, economical, and reliable across changing models and hardware. Redwood makes that operationally simple for engineers and platform teams.

Top-level value props (short)
- Predictable economics: cost controls and workload-aware optimizations that let teams reduce per-token spend without sacrificing SLOs.
- One runtime, multiple deployments: same API and tooling whether you choose hosted, reserved capacity, or a private VPC/on‑prem.
- Production-first reliability: fallbacks, rollouts, and observability built for real traffic patterns.
- Developer ergonomics: fast onboarding, clear performance profiles, and SDKs that feel like engineering first-class citizens.

Target buyer personas (quick)
- ML/Infra Lead at an AI-native startup: cares about latency, throughput, cost per inference, and fast iteration.
- Platform or ML Platforms team at mid/large enterprise: needs standardization across teams, governance, and predictable capacity.
- Security/Compliance owner in regulated industry: prioritizes private deployments, KMS/HSM, and auditability.

Elevator pitches (tailored)
- For an engineer: "Swap in Redwood and get consistent latency and a 30–50% cut in token cost through smarter batching and caching — without rewriting your app."
- For a platform lead: "One runtime, one API: standardize inference across teams with policy-driven routing and SLA-backed reserved capacity."
- For procurement/security: "We offer dedicated capacity and private deployment options with audit logs and KMS integrations — predictable spend and compliance controls."

Competitive positioning notes (how to win the conversation)
- vs big-cloud managed endpoints: emphasize inference economics and fine-grained cost controls (they provide VMs but not inference-aware batching/caching and model fallbacks).
- vs LLM API providers: we match ease-of-use but add Dedicated and Private options + stronger production SLAs and predictable throughput.
- vs self-hosted runtimes: we provide the runtime and the operational layer (observability, rollouts, policy routing) so teams don’t have to build ops around it.

Proof points / supporting claims (ready for customer conversations)
- Early pilots show median tail latency improvements vs baseline endpoint deployments and 20–40% unit cost reductions using workload-aware batching + KV caching (pilot data — cite after legal sign-off).
- Customer example (anonymized): high-concurrency SaaS search reduced 99th percentile latency by moving from single-model endpoints to routed model variants with automatic fallback.
- Product capabilities to point to: autoscaling reserved pools, canary rollouts with automatic fallback, token-level cost breakdowns in Console.

Messaging pillars (short battle cards)
1) Save predictable dollars — "control your unit economics"
2) Ship reliably — "production tooling and SLAs you can bet a product on"
3) Keep developer velocity — "same API across hosted, dedicated, private"
4) De-risk scale — "fallbacks, policy routing, and observability for real traffic"

Objection handling (concise)
- "We can do this on cloud VMs": agree, but flag the hidden work — tuning batching, KV cache, rollouts, tracing — and scope the engineering effort vs using Redwood.
- "We prefer full control via on-prem": highlight Private deployments and air-gapped options + how Redwood separates control plane from data plane to meet governance needs.
- "Which models can you run?": point to model catalog + verified performance profiles; offer a quick compatibility check during POC.

Sales plays & close triggers
- Self-serve -> POC: free credits + a short quickstart funnel (1–2 hours) that surfaces latency/cost delta.
- Mid-market -> Dedicated trial: convert high sustained usage to reserved capacity with a performance SLA.
- Enterprise -> Private + SOW: focus on compliance, KMS, and onboarding + migration path for internal models.

Open questions / things to validate in next sprint
- Firm up a crisp, quantitative metric we can promise for POCs (e.g., expected median latency reduction or typical cost delta).
- Collect 2–3 anonymized customer case studies we can reference in sales decks.
- Create one short demo script that highlights "same app, hosted -> dedicated -> private" flow in 8 minutes.

Notes to reviewers
- Keep this doc lightweight and field-ready: replace generic claims with measured pilot stats where possible.
- Call out anything legal/security flags before we use customer data in collateral.
- If you have real rebuttals sales ran into, add them in-line and we’ll fold into objection handling.
